assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling is a general bond-forming method that turned aryl amine construction from a harsh, substrate-limited problem into a routine step; its use in pharmaceutical process and discovery chemistry and in countless total syntheses is directly visible in the literature. Strong chemical novelty (ligand design enabling amine coupling) and high lasting impact, which is the kind of general method I weight most.
assessment.attribution: Hartwig and Buchwald independently developed the decisive catalyst systems and ligand generations that made the reaction general. Kosugi/Migita tin-amide precedent is earlier and arguably needs acknowledgment, but a two-person prize is fair and clean.
assessment.maturity: Mature: four decades of independent confirmation, industrial scale use, and a stable mechanistic understanding. The 2010 cross-coupling prize covered C-C coupling, so a C-N prize is a follow-on and some members may see it as partly redundant.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2010 Nobel Prize for Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling may be seen as reducing novelty.
Precise credit to Kosugi/Migita-type precedent is uncertain to me from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened radical and open-shell reactivity under mild conditions with simple light sources and became a general synthetic platform, widely adopted in medicinal chemistry and in late-stage functionalization. A real conceptual shift in how chemists make bonds.
assessment.attribution: Credit is diffuse: MacMillan (already a laureate for organocatalysis in 2021), Yoon, Stephenson, Nicewicz, Melchiorre, Konig, Fukuzumi and earlier inorganic photochemists. I propose Yoon, Stephenson and Nicewicz as the early organic-synthesis pioneers, but the allocation is contestable and excluding MacMillan is a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed and broadly adopted over about fifteen years; some fraction of the literature is incremental, and reproducibility and scalability of certain photochemical protocols vary. Timing is plausible.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would credit MacMillan again alongside the others is unresolved.
Priority versus earlier inorganic photochemistry (Kellogg, Fukuzumi, Konig) is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective C-H functionalization changes retrosynthetic logic by treating ubiquitous C-H bonds as functional handles; directing-group, ligand- and template-controlled methods are now used in drug discovery and natural product synthesis. High conceptual importance for step efficiency.
assessment.attribution: Yu (ligand-accelerated and template-controlled meta/remote activation), Sanford (Pd(II/IV) chemistry and directed functionalization) and Hartwig (borylation and related) made distinct decisive contributions; Bergman/Smith/Daugulis show a broad field with several possible split points. Three-person prize is plausible but the boundary of what is recognized is fuzzy.
assessment.maturity: Substantial confirmation and use, though practicality in industry is still developing compared with cross-coupling; timing is arguably slightly early for the full scope but not premature for the core ideas.
uncertainties: Compound field with several distinct sub-discoveries; a coherent prize citation is hard.
Hartwig also appears under C-N coupling, so he could not be double counted.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolation of stable carbenes showed that nucleophilic carbenes are bottleable and led to N-heterocyclic carbenes as ubiquitous ligands and organocatalysts, deeply influencing olefin metathesis catalysts, cross-coupling and main-group chemistry. Clear, original and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Arduengo isolated the first crystalline NHC (1991) and Bertrand the earlier stable phosphino-silyl carbene (1988), so priority is a real issue; Bertrand also pioneered cyclic alkyl amino carbenes. Two-person prize is natural; other credited names (Nolan, Rovis, Bode) are application developers.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of confirmation; recognition if anything is late.
uncertainties: Priority between Bertrand 1988 carbene and Arduengo 1991 NHC needs careful citation wording.
Partial overlap with 2005 and 2021 prizes in how catalysis is framed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base into another on DNA without double-strand breaks, a genuinely new chemical tool with rapid translational uptake, including clinical trials. Conceptually clean and impactful, though the nearest Nobel was the 2020 CRISPR prize, so I ask what is new chemically: here the answer is engineered deaminase chemistry on genomic DNA.
assessment.attribution: Komor and Gaudelli were the lead scientists on cytosine and adenine base editors in the Liu lab; Liu led the invention. A three-person configuration is supportable; Nishida and Kondo's earlier deaminase-CRISPR work complicates priority.
assessment.maturity: Young but already confirmed by many labs and first clinical results; slightly early relative to the long-term safety record.
uncertainties: Relation to CRISPR prize and Medicine/Chemistry boundary.
Priority of Nishida/Kondo concurrent report is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed that main-group combinations can activate H2 and other small molecules without metals, a surprising and general concept that spawned metal-free hydrogenation and a broad field in main-group catalysis.
assessment.attribution: Stephan reported the first metal-free reversible H2 activation (2006) and developed the concept; Erker contributed key mechanistic and structural work and the geminal FLP chemistry. Two-person prize is a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed conceptually; practical synthetic impact (e.g., in industry) has been more limited than the conceptual impact, which weighs against it for me.
uncertainties: Industrial adoption of FLP hydrogenation remains modest.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation made chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins routine by joining unprotected peptides chemoselectively, enabling synthesis of proteins with defined modifications. A clear methodological advance with lasting impact in chemical biology.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson developed the original NCL (1994); Muir pioneered expressed protein ligation, extending it to semisynthesis. Danishefsky and Brik/Liu extended it. A Kent-Dawson-Muir configuration is reasonable though not unique.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely used for decades; the field could be viewed as a long-running tool rather than a transformation of mainstream synthesis.
uncertainties: Overlap with Merrifield 1984 prize for solid-phase peptide synthesis may reduce novelty in some eyes.
Allocation between Kent and Dawson on priority is not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues introduces a new pharmacological modality built on chemically designed heterobifunctional molecules; many clinical-stage compounds. Chemistry is mostly medicinal and I would judge it by what is new chemically, which is the design principle rather than a reaction.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies founded the PROTAC concept; Ciulli contributed VHL ligands and structure-based design; Handa/Ito established the thalidomide cereblon mechanism for glues. The attribution is split between PROTACs and molecular glues, which could require separate recognition.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is still emerging, so it is somewhat early; no approved PROTAC drug as far as I know, so I am uncertain on this point.
uncertainties: No approved degrader drug confirmed in my knowledge.
Compound discovery with two sub-discoveries and a large credit set.
